description: Classification of the usual Kubernetes platform components, for clusters that run them. Separate from the base preset because it is an opinion about specific software, not about update types - a repository that runs none of this should not inherit it.

The names are here rather than in each repository because what they are does not change between clusters: Longhorn owns volumes wherever it runs, and external-dns owns nothing wherever it runs. Anything whose meaning IS local - an image built in-repo, a version pinned to match another component, a node upgraded by hand - belongs to the repository, not here.

packageRules.description: Owns no data: the worst case is a revert and a resync, not a restore. cert-manager qualifies because a failed issuance leaves the existing certificate serving until someone fixes it.
Storage and secrets: a bad upgrade takes the data with it, and a revert does not bring it back.

Longhorn supports one minor step at a time and enforces it: its manager, webhook and recovery-backend pods refuse to start on an unsupported path rather than warn. A single PR that skips a minor therefore takes the storage control plane down instead of upgrading it. One PR per minor keeps the path walkable, and it leaves the group above so a storage upgrade is never bundled with anything else.
Postgres: operator, cluster chart and backup plugin move together or not at all.
Databases upgrade their own on-disk state on first start, so swapping the image is not a revertable change.
Ingress and SSO: breaking either one locks everything behind it out, including the GitOps controller used to fix it.
GitOps itself: a broken upgrade cannot be fixed by the thing that is broken.
CRDs are cluster-scoped and are not pruned on downgrade, so a revert leaves the new schema in place.
Operators carry reconciliation state and own the resources they manage; a bad version acts on every instance at once.
